trust_decision.summary: Whether a browser may render the WebUI/RPC responses inside a cross-origin frame; decided by response headers set (after the fix) once at the top of the single libevent general callback handle_request, which every Transmission-generated response passes through.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the WebUI and RPC response paths; handle_request already sets the shared 'Server' header on output_headers for all responses, the obvious place to add X-Frame-Options/CSP.

fix_sites.entry_point: none directly; new helper add_clickjacking_prevention_headers (fix.diff:17-22) called only from handle_request
fix_sites.module_kind: internal helper in the RPC/HTTP server module

fix_sites.entry_point: any HTTP request to the RPC server (GET /transmission/web/*, POST /transmission/rpc, OPTIONS, redirects, 401/403/404/409/421 replies) via evhttp_set_gencb at libtransmission/rpc-server.cc:829

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Only one HTTP server exists in the tree (evhttp_new only at libtransmission/rpc-server.cc:793); web/ contains no server code.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only responses not covered are ones libevent generates itself before handle_request runs (e.g. methods rejected by evhttp_set_allowed_methods at libtransmission/rpc-server.cc:795); a solver can fairly say these are library error pages with no UI to clickjack.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: CORS for RPC clients: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' and the OPTIONS preflight path must keep working; a fix that adds a restrictive CSP beyond frame-ancestors, or blocks cross-origin requests, would break third-party RPC clients. This is weak: frame headers do not interact with CORS.

O6_input_shapes: all responses from handle_request (web file 200, RPC JSON 200/204, OPTIONS 200, 301 redirect, 401/403/404/405/409/421 simple responses); no input-shape dimension

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Error replies that libevent's evhttp builds itself (disallowed method, malformed request) never reach handle_request, so they carry no frame headers
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are library-generated error pages with no interactive content to frame, and Transmission cannot add headers to them without patching libevent
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the behaviour is inside third-party libevent

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make send_simple_response build its own fresh header set, or add a second early-exit path before the helper call, so HTML error/info pages (421 host-whitelist page, 409 session-id page) miss the headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both are HTML pages with links, built separately from the file and JSON paths; a maintainer could easily have set headers only on the success paths.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A separate static-file server (e.g. a dedicated web-client listener or callback) that serves index.html without going through handle_request
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Serving the web client from its own evhttp_set_cb is a common libevent idiom. It would be a where-type sibling only, though.

O9_family: Missing anti-framing response headers (clickjacking, CWE-1021); the CWE-113 label on the advisory does not match the fix

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C++20 compiler; bundled third-party deps (libevent, libdeflate, fmt) under third-party/
O10_build.project_tests: tests/libtransmission/rpc-test.cc exists but does not test the HTTP layer; no test under tests/ references rpc-server, handle_request or evhttp

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add X-Frame-Options only in serve_file (libtransmission/rpc-server.cc:294), leaving redirect/error HTML pages and RPC responses without it. Still close to a correct fix.

out_of_scope_notes: OPTIONS preflight echoes the client's Access-Control-Request-Headers value back into a response header (libtransmission/rpc-server.cc:559-562); libevent's header validation was not checked. Not pursued.
unverified: Exactly which libevent-internal error replies bypass the general callback was not checked in the libevent source
Recall risk judged low from the recent publication date and small fix; not checked against public write-ups
